summary: This RFC defines the "AC Glue" YANG model, which augments LxVPN service and network models with references to attachment circuits, letting a provider tie Layer 2/3 VPN services to the underlying AC infrastructure.

plainLanguage.summary: Glue sticks two pieces together. This model links the VPN service descriptions to the descriptions of the customer links.

questions: link vpn service models to attachment circuits
what is the ietf-ac-glue yang module
how to bind vpn service to attachment circuit
subtitle: A YANG module that lets VPN service and network models point at attachment circuits managed separately.

tldr.problem: Operators who sell Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs also need to manage the attachment circuits (ACs) that connect customers to the provider network, but the existing VPN models had no standard way to refer to ACs created elsewhere.
tldr.mechanism: The "ietf-ac-glue" YANG module augments the L2SM, L3SM, L2NM and L3NM with references to ACs created through the AC service model (RFC 9834) and, for the network models, the AC network model (RFC 9835).
tldr.outcome: AC provisioning can be separated from VPN service provisioning, and a VPN can be bound to ACs that already exist or are created later. The RFC is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 9836 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2025. It has not been obsoleted or updated, so it is the current definition of the ietf-ac-glue module.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
For data to flow within a provider network, the links between customer termination points and the provider (usually via a Provider Edge, PE) need the right setup. The RFC calls that setup an attachment circuit (AC), and the underlying link the bearer.

The document specifies the ietf-ac-glue YANG module. It updates existing service and network VPN modules with the information needed to bind specific services to ACs created with the AC service model of RFC 9834. The augmented modules are the L2VPN Service Model (L2SM, RFC 8466), the L3VPN Service Model (L3SM, RFC 8299), the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM, RFC 9291) and the L3VPN Network Model (L3NM, RFC 9182). The L2NM and L3NM are also augmented with references to ACs managed with the AC network model of RFC 9835.

The module conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342.
sections.plainLanguage: A VPN is like a private road between two places, and an attachment circuit is the driveway that connects your house to it. This document gives the road map a way to say which driveway it uses.

sections.title: How the AC Models Fit Together
sections.content:
The RFC describes a small family of AC modules. ietf-ac-common (RFC 9833) is imported by ietf-bearer-svc, ietf-ac-svc and ietf-ac-ntw. Bearers managed with ietf-bearer-svc can be referenced by service ACs managed with ietf-ac-svc, and a bearer can list the ACs that use it.

To correlate an AC service request with the AC actually provisioned in the network, ietf-ac-ntw uses the AC references exposed by ietf-ac-svc. Finally, to bind Layer 2 or Layer 3 VPN services to ACs, ietf-ac-glue augments the service and network VPN models with the service references from ietf-ac-svc and the network references from ietf-ac-ntw.

Prefixes used in the module are ac-svc, ac-ntw, l2nm, l2vpn-svc, l3nm and l3vpn-svc.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of a set of building blocks where each block describes one thing: the cable, the link, or the real setup. The glue block is the one that connects the VPN blocks to the link blocks.

sections.title: Sample Uses
sections.content:
The RFC lists several ways ACs can be arranged. A Customer Edge (CE) can be a physical device or a logical entity such as a virtual service function. A single AC can be bound to one or several peer Service Attachment Points (SAPs), and a single CE can terminate several ACs on the same bearer or on distinct bearers. Customers may also ask for protection schemes where their ACs end on the same PE or on distinct PEs, and the provider uses that request to decide where to terminate the AC and whether to enable capabilities such as the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP).

The second use is separating AC provisioning from VPN provisioning. A single AC may host several connectivity services, for example an L2VPN, an L3VPN or a Network Slice Service. To avoid interference and redundant information, a provider can expose an interface to manage ACs network-wide. Customers then request an AC (ietf-ac-svc) and later refer to it when requesting VPN services (ietf-ac-glue). Network controllers can likewise use ietf-ac-ntw references to glue the L2NM or L3NM to the relevant ACs.
sections.plainLanguage: You can build the driveway first and decide later which roads it joins. Or one driveway can serve several roads at once.

sections.title: The Module Tree and Augmentations
sections.content:
The RFC maps existing VPN concepts onto ACs. In the L3SM a site-network-access maps to an AC with both Layer 2 and Layer 3 properties, in the L2SM to an AC with Layer 2 properties, and the vpn-network-access of the L3NM and L2NM maps to an AC per RFC 9834 or RFC 9835.

The module adds a leaf-list named ac-svc-ref on the site network accesses of the L2SM and L3SM, and a single ac-svc-ref leaf on each site-network-access, guarded by the ac-glue feature. For the L2NM and L3NM it adds, on the VPN network accesses, an ac-svc-ref leaf-list plus an ac-ntw-ref list keyed by ac-ref with node-ref and network-ref, and the single-access counterparts.

The module can reference ACs inside or outside an individual VPN network access, to cover deployments where the AC reference is created before or after the VPN instance.

When an AC is referenced within a specific network access, that AC information takes precedence over any overlapping information given for the same network access.
sections.plainLanguage: It adds a little label slot to each VPN entry where you can write the name of the driveway. If the label and the VPN entry disagree, the label wins.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
Appendix A.1 uses a VPWS topology with two PEs, each serving two CEs, and four ACs named AC1 to AC4. The L2NM request references each AC inside the matching vpn-network-access using ietf-ac-glue:ac-svc-ref.

Appendix A.2 starts with bearers 1234 and 5678 already in place. The provider first creates two ACs, ac-1 and ac-2, with the AC service model, sharing a profile with C-VLAN 550, an MTU of 1550 and a CIR of 20480000. A customer then asks for a VPLS instance with identifier 1543 through the L2NM, referencing ac-1 and ac-2 outside any single network access. The provider orchestrator may first check feasibility with the SAP model (RFC 9408), and the AC network model can then return the provisioned AC details.
sections.plainLanguage: First the provider builds two driveways. Then a customer orders a private road and just says which two driveways it should join.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module follows the YANG security template. Management protocols such as NETCONF and RESTCONF have to use a secure transport layer and mutual authentication, and the Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM, RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

The writable nodes ac-svc-ref and ac-ntw-ref are sensitive. An attacker who can modify or delete the ACs bound to a running service can break the service and cause Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations; monitoring configuration changes can detect this. For reads, the references hold no privacy data per se, but ac-svc-ref may be used to track the set of VPN instances in which a customer takes part. Unlike ac-svc-ref, ac-ntw-ref is unique within a node and may multiplex many peer CEs.
sections.plainLanguage: If a bad person could change the labels, they could unplug your driveway from the road. So only trusted people should be allowed to edit them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-ac-glue in the IETF XML Registry (RFC 3688), with the IESG as registrant. It also registered the YANG module ietf-ac-glue with prefix ac-glue in the YANG Module Names registry, referencing RFC 9836.
sections.plainLanguage: The module got an official name in a public list so nobody else uses the same name.

layers.label: Customer
layers.detail: Uses customer service models such as ietf-l2vpn-svc, ietf-l3vpn-svc, ietf-ac-svc, ietf-ac-glue and ietf-bearer-svc

layers.label: Service Orchestration
layers.detail: Uses network models such as ietf-l2vpn-ntw, ietf-l3vpn-ntw, ietf-sap-ntw, ietf-ac-glue and ietf-ac-ntw

layers.label: Domain Orchestration
layers.detail: Uses device configuration models via a config manager (NETCONF/CLI)
